title: People missed that Abraham laughed at God’s promise too (Genesis 17:17)
paragraphs: People missed that Abraham laughed at God’s promise too (Genesis 17:17)
Sarah wasn’t the only one who laughed.

Abraham laughed too.
Face down. Old body. Impossible promise.
And in that moment, even the father of faith blinked at the size of God’s word.
Genesis 17:17 does not hide it. Abraham laughed and said in his heart, “Shall a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old?” The Bible is honest about its heroes. That matters.

Because faith is not pretending you never stagger.
Faith is hearing the impossible… and still staying under the voice of God until the promise becomes bigger than your doubt.

Abraham laughed.
Sarah laughed.
Yet God still moved.

Not because their faith was flawless.
Because His covenant was.

That is the Gospel pattern all over Scripture. We tremble. We question. We fail. But God remains faithful. He does not save perfect people. He keeps His word to weak people through His own power. And that story reaches its fullness in Jesus Christ—the promised Son through whom barren hearts become alive again.

So yes, Abraham laughed.
And grace did not walk away.

It stayed.
It spoke again.
It fulfilled what human strength could never produce.

That means your moment of weakness does not have to be the end of your story. Bring your unbelief to God. Bring your fear to Christ. Repent of cynicism, yes—but do not run from Him. The same God who answered Abraham has given us an even greater promise in Jesus: forgiveness for sinners, new life for the dead soul, and hope that does not collapse under impossibility.
